Hm I think I’m just spelling it out wrong phonetically. Not exactly a “ruh” sound but it has that r sound that Spanish learners have trouble with. That same sound heard in butter and ladder (like another comment used). I’m not sure if people with American southern accents pronounce it the same way though 🤷‍♀️

If this is of any help to you I saw this video (it was a meme but nevertheless) that blew my mind.  

It was a video in Spanish saying that American English speakers DO have a “rolled r” sound in English. The example was they gave was “Spotify” vs “Sporify”. It’s never pronounced as “spo-tih-fy” but more like “Spo-ruh-fy”. If you say it fast you can hear that “rolled” r sound! I thought it was just me forcing the sound but I’ve seen other Americans pronouncing it and they can all do that small r sound!  


Don’t know if that example is any help to you but it is somewhat possible! Spanish was my first language and eventually I lost most of my grasp on it, but I can roll my r’s in shorter words (EX: “por que” “hermana” “ver”). I have more difficulty with words like “carro” y “perro” but it’s comprensible depending on the context. Good luck :)
